name: Remembering and Using Information
gist: Papers about helping agents remember important facts and use them later, like keeping notes of what happened and learning from experience.
explain: An agent that forgets everything it learned is inefficient, because it wastes time and compute by re-discovering the same patterns over and over. These papers focus on how agents can remember facts, previous experiences, and patterns, then use that memory to make better decisions so they improve with time. Imagine you ask an AI assistant to help you over multiple weeks, and every time you talk to it, it has to re-learn what you care about, who your collaborators are, and what projects you are working on — that is frustrating and slow. Better agents maintain context: they remember you, what you asked last time, what you learned together, which means they can pick up where you left off without starting over. The papers here tackle how to build memory systems that agents can actually tap into when solving new problems.

The challenge is that memory is finite and messy. An agent can't remember everything — at some point it has to forget old information or pick what matters most. Also, remembering something is only useful if the agent knows when and how to apply it. If an agent encounters a problem similar to one it solved before, does it recognize the similarity? Does it look up the old solution? Does it retrieve just the relevant parts, not everything? There is also a trade-off: detailed memory takes more time to search, sparse memory misses important connections. And if the agent stores wrong information, then later uses it, the mistake compounds.

Papers here work on memory architectures — different ways to organize what an agent remembers. Some use explicit memory systems like stored facts or a log of past conversations, which makes the memory searchable and auditable. Others use learned representations that capture the essence of experience, which compresses memory so it is faster to use. Some focus on retrieval — given a new problem, how does the agent find relevant past experiences quickly without searching through everything? Others focus on integration — once the agent finds a past solution or lesson, how does it apply it to the current situation and adapt if things are different? The goal is agents that learn cumulatively, where every experience makes them a little better at their job instead of being thrown away, so they get smarter the more they work.

papers.title: BrowseNet: Knowledge Graph-Based Associative Memory for Contextual Information Retrieval
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art exact match performance over graph-based RAG approaches and dense retrieval methods.

papers.title: De-Linearizing Agent Traces: Bayesian Inference of Latent Partial Orders for Efficient Execution
papers.contribution: Recovers dependency structure more accurately than baselines and enables a compiled executor that prunes irrelevant context, yielding substantial reductions in token usage and execution time.

papers.title: MonoScale: Scaling Multi-Agent System with Monotonic Improvement
papers.contribution: Achieves stable performance gains as agent pool grows on GAIA and Humanity's Last Exam benchmarks, outperforming naive scale-up with monotonic non-decreasing performance guarantee under non-interfering expansion.

papers.title: REMem: Reasoning with Episodic Memory in Language Agent
papers.contribution: Outperforms Mem0 and HippoRAG by 3.4% and 13.4% on episodic recollection and reasoning tasks respectively, with more robust refusal behavior.

papers.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing memory mechanisms on web browsing and software engineering tasks, enabling agents to self-evolve and exhibit emergent behaviors.

papers.title: AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications
papers.contribution: Shows that causality-graph-based memory with tool-augmented retrieval (AMA-Agent) achieves 57.22% accuracy, outperforming baselines by 11.16% on realistic agentic memory tasks.

papers.title: AdaMEM: Test-Time Adaptive Memory for Language Agents
papers.contribution: AdaMEM achieves up to 13% gains on ALFWorld, 11% on WebShop, and consistent leading performance on HotpotQA, enabling continuous reasoning and self-evolution post-deployment.

papers.title: AssoMem: Scalable Memory QA with Multi-Signal Associative Retrieval
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three benchmarks including the newly introduced MeetingQA dataset.

papers.title: ContextNav: Towards Agentic Multimodal In-Context Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across various datasets, demonstrating the promise of agentic workflows for advancing scalable multimodal in-context learning.

papers.title: DAMR: Efficient and Adaptive Context-Aware Knowledge Graph Question Answering with LLM-Guided MCTS
papers.contribution: Achieves efficient and context-aware KGQA through LLM-guided MCTS reducing search space while maintaining evaluation accuracy.

papers.title: DeepImageSearch: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Context-Aware Image Retrieval in Visual Histories
papers.contribution: Constructs DISBench, a benchmark showing state-of-the-art models significantly struggle with context-dependent queries, demonstrating the necessity of agentic reasoning in next-generation retrieval systems.

papers.title: Embodied Agents Meet Personalization: Investigating Challenges and Solutions Through the Lens of Memory Utilization
papers.contribution: A hierarchical knowledge graph-based user-profile memory module achieves substantial improvements on single and joint-memory tasks by managing personalized knowledge separately.

papers.title: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art by 19.6% on AndroidWorld while reducing token costs 6x relative to GPT-4o with 2.8s average latency.

papers.title: Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic–Procedural Memory
papers.contribution: H-EPM delivers up to 50%+ inference-time gains over baselines and up to 40%+ improvement on multi-turn tool-use benchmarks with out-of-distribution generalization.

papers.title: Experience-based Knowledge Correction for Robust Planning in Minecraft
papers.contribution: XENON surpasses prior agents in knowledge learning and long-horizon planning on multiple Minecraft benchmarks, even with 7B LLM.

papers.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
papers.contribution: Improves frameworks like SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher by up to 17.06%, with strong cross-task and cross-LLM generalization, substantially reducing agent-environment interactions.

papers.title: Multimodal Policy Internalization for Conversational Agents
papers.contribution: Enables stronger policy-following without in-context policies, addressing data and algorithmic challenges of multimodal policy internalization.

papers.title: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms task-agnostic and task-specific baselines across three heterogeneous benchmarks while achieving highest information density under information-theoretic analysis.

papers.title: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
papers.contribution: SE-GA achieves 89.0% on ScreenSpot and 75.8% on AndroidControl-High, with superior generalization on AndroidWorld benchmark.

papers.title: Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Skill-Pro achieves superior skill reuse rates and significant gains with extreme memory compression, enabling transparent accumulation and refinement of procedural knowledge for long-term autonomy.

papers.title: XSkill: Continual Learning from Experience and Skills in Multimodal Agents
papers.contribution: Consistently and substantially outperforms tool-only and learning baselines across five benchmarks, with complementary knowledge streams showing superior zero-shot generalization.
